eventDescription: Easy access footpaths are dotted across fifty acres of natural, species-rich wildflower meadows. eventName: Darts Farm Pumpkin Fest - Half Term Fun
eventDescription: Every October, Darts Farm transforms into something quite different from its usual self — tens of thousands of homegrown pumpkins filling the fields in every shape, size and shade of orange imaginable, with enough going on around them to make a proper afternoon of it. Magic shows, game shows, live music, roaming performers, marshmallow toasting, face painting and s’mores are all part of the mix, with the farm’s natural backdrop doing a lot of the atmospheric heavy lifting. They do go all out, and it certainly provides the pumpkin-patch fix most families are looking for - with the world's 3rd biggest pumpkin in residence no less! With the usual Darts playarea directly opposite, and all the amenities of the farm shop and cafes, and quick access to the Exe Estuary trail for a walk, it's a classic take on a Pumpkin Patch but with lots you can add on easily. Like most pumpkin patches, the ticket price covers entry but not the pumpkin itself, which you choose and pay for separately on the day; some activities carry an additional charge and tend to sit at a price point similar to others (the standard eye-watering extras, but hard to avoid when they're placed under children's noses). The farm runs on booked arrival slots throughout October, with the busiest dates around half term selling out well in advance — worth getting tickets sorted early if you have a specific weekend in mind.

eventDescription: Pumpkin Fest at Strawberry Fields is one of the most involved autumn pumpkin-themed events in Devon, built around homegrown pumpkins, seasonal displays and family entertainment (and everything pumpkin-themed you can possibly think of!) rather than just a quick pick-your-own stop. The pumpkin patch gives children the simple job of choosing their own pumpkin, while the wider site adds barrel train rides, photo displays, acoustic live music, magic shows, circus shows and plenty of autumn food. There are marshmallows to roast (additional cost), countless photo opportunities, lots of tasty autumnal food, face painting (additional cost) as well as lots more. Most things do include an additional cost on top of your entry ticket, but there is enough going on to make the visit feel like a seasonal day out, moving between pumpkins, performances, food stalls and the wider farm shop setting. Arrival time slots should be booked online ahead of time (they book up quickly) but there isn't a fixed limit on how long visitors can stay once inside, but you likely want to allow a couple of hours minimum to make the most of the trip. The ground is mainly woodchip-covered, with the pumpkin patch in a field, so mud and uneven surfaces are part of the experience after wet weather. Food is a big part of the event, with options including loaded fries, burgers, pizzas, ice cream, donuts, bakery treats, pick and mix, coffee stations and a bar.

eventDescription: Sanctuary flower farm and pick-your-own tucked within the Froginwell Estate, is a wonderful new addition to East Devon and is open on Sundays and Mondays from May through to October. Entry is £5 per adult (under 12's and over 70's go free) and covers both the flower farm and 20 acres of meadow walks across the estate itself. The rows of cut flowers — dahlias, sweet peas, sunflowers, zinnias and seasonal blooms — are there to be wandered through and picked from at your own pace (for an additional cost of £25 per bucket), with stems wrapped in paper to take home or transported in a refillable bucket (incl. in the cost), which keeps them fresh for the journey. The CoffeeBox on site covers coffee, hot drinks and snacks, set under a large bell-tent canopy with views across the flower fields; it's a very pretty, photogenic setting with friendly staff on-hand who are genuinely passionate about floristry and helping you build a beautiful bouquet. A seasonal pass for £20 gives unlimited access on open days throughout the season with 10% off flowers - potentially handy if you live locally and can imagine coming back across the summer with friends, or to treat someone for a special occasion.

eventDescription: Greendale’s Pumpkin Patch turns the farm shop into a seasonal autumn stop, with pumpkins to choose, photo spots around the patch and the wider Greendale site close by for food, animals and the Farm Trail. The pumpkin picking itself is simple and open-ended: visitors can wander, compare shapes and sizes, choose one to take home and make the visit feel part of the build-up to Halloween rather than a big-ticket day out. Unlike some pumpkin experiences that charge for every element, this one is genuinely free to walk around — you choose your pumpkin and pay only for what you take home and the pricing is clear and upfront. The free Pumpkin Trail adds a second layer, with clue sheets from Oscar’s and pumpkins hidden around the Farm Trail and Farm Shop, ending with a sweet treat once the challenge is complete. Entry to the pumpkin patch is free and works really well alongside a wander around to look at the animal pens.

eventDescription: Run by Amelia and Giles, who are raising their own three children on the farm, there's a relaxed and genuinely welcoming atmosphere here that's hard to manufacture and easy to feel the moment you arrive. The farm sits in a quiet valley between Newton Abbot and Shaldon, with fields of pesticide-free heirloom flowers — dahlias, sweet peas, sunflowers and scented varieties that change through the season — grown slowly and available to pick at your own pace with a pair of snips. Children who are unmoved by the flowers tend to find their own reasons to stay: miniature ponies, pigs (including the much-loved Cris-P-Bacon), swings that even pre-teens apparently can't resist, and the simple freedom of roaming a working farm without a fixed route. The Flower Barn café does homemade cakes and good coffee with views across the fields, and a short walk through the farm brings you down to the River Teign if legs need stretching further.
